answer: Persistent neighborhood pulse. Each agent periodically emits a signed timing pulse to a fixed set of neighbors; the network only routes work to agents whose pulse arrives within a narrow phase window relative to a reef of stable, long-lived peers. A newcomer must sustain continuous, phase-consistent contact across many cycles before it is admitted to the timing reef. Sybil clusters share one timing source and drift out of phase, so they must run distinct, always-on infrastructure with independent clocks and continuous uptime to fake a raven of steady pulses,
